ops.title: yclaw secret reconcile — deferred secret-hygiene hardenings
ops.body:
Two real-but-deferred hardenings in the new `yclaw secret reconcile` credential path (fable review 2026-07-19, ranked CONSIDER not MUST_FIX). Both are same-user-observer threat-model and mirror the retired bash `scripts/lib/secrets.sh`, so deferring them is not a regression.

1. **Secrets transit `security` argv.** `yclaw/keychain.py` passes the keychain unlock password (`unlock-keychain -p`) and every secret value (`add-generic-password -w`, and `ensure()`'s create/seed) on the argv of the `security` process — readable via `ps` by any same-user process for the duration of the call. This bites harder here than usual because the project's stated boundary is that same-user agent sessions cannot read the keychain (login-keychain unsearchability), yet an agent polling `ps` during the operator's Terminal.app `reconcile` captures everything. **Fix if pursued:** `security -i` batch mode reads commands from stdin, keeping values off argv. Not closed because it needs an active same-user observer with lucky timing and a malicious same-user process has other paths (PATH shims) this alone doesn't close.

2. **sops encrypt writes full bundle plaintext to a temp file.** `yclaw/sops.py encrypt()` (and reconcile's canonical-plaintext render) write the decrypted bundle plaintext to a `NamedTemporaryFile` (0600 in a per-user 0700 TMPDIR); a SIGKILL between write and cleanup leaves every host secret in plaintext on disk. **Fix if pursued:** pipe via `sops --encrypt /dev/stdin` (existing `--input-type yaml`) to remove the at-rest window entirely.

Fixed in the same review (MUST_FIX): `keychain.ensure()` order swap (login-item write before create-keychain), `--rotate SECRET` fail-loud on uncovered owners, atomic `os.replace()` bundle writes. Accepted by design: authkey never auto-minted when a prior bundle value exists (reuse + warn; `--rotate-authkey` is the escape hatch).

Also live at review time: **codex/gpt-5.6-sol lanes down (401 refresh-token revoked)** — `codex login` needed to restore the finder/refuter and sol implementation lanes; until then those route to fable/opus.
